instruction: I'm feeling a bit lonely. Do you think having siblings helps with that?
reply: Expect it, name it, and do not argue them out of it: "it's hard having someone new in the house" lands better than "you love your sister really". Give the older one ten minutes a day that belong to nobody else, let them help with the baby only if they offer to, and blame the baby for nothing they can hear - "the baby needs me" rather than "you'll have to wait".

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated, but I drink a lot of coffee. Does caffeine affect hydration?
reply: No, not in ordinary amounts: a cup of tea or coffee is mostly water, and the caffeine in it makes you pass only a little more than the drink gave you, so it counts towards your fluids. The six-to-eight-glasses figure includes them.

instruction: I'm looking for a new vacation destination. Can you suggest some adventure spots?
reply: Pick one shape and put a time on it, because a free day with no plan turns into the sofa. The ones that cost nothing: a walk with a destination (a park, a canal, a hill, a shop that sells something you like), a free museum or gallery - most have a permanent collection that costs nothing - and the library, which has events, papers and warmth.

instruction: I'm learning about animal adaptations in school. Can you tell me about how polar bears stay warm?
reply: Cold or strong emotion makes tiny muscles pull your hairs upright, which traps a layer of air for warmth and made our furry ancestors look bigger. We have kept the reflex even though we no longer have the fur for it to work.

instruction: I'm looking for a new game to play. What's popular in esports right now?
reply: Search for the sport plus your town and 'club', then email and ask about a taster session: most clubs have a beginners' or social night that costs a few pounds. Turn up to that rather than a match, and say you're new — clubs are used to it, and it's the fastest way to find people at your level.

instruction: I'm new to the gym and I want to start a workout routine. What's a good exercise for beginners?
reply: Add weight when you can hit the top of your rep range on every set with clean form - usually every week or two when you are new. Take the smallest jump you have, 2.5kg on a bar or the next dumbbell up, and expect to lose a rep or two for a session or so; that is the new weight working, not a bad day.

instruction: I'm looking for a place to watch the game this weekend. Do you know any good sports bars near me?
reply: Pick the team someone you already watch with supports, or the one nearest to where you live — going to games matters more than the badge. Watch a few matches first and let it happen; supporting a team is mostly habit plus the people you watch it with.

instruction: I'm looking for information about vintage sports equipment. What's one of the most valuable vintage sports items?
reply: Start with very little: trainers or astro boots, shorts or leggings, a water bottle and, for football or hockey, shin pads. Clubs lend sticks, bats and bibs to beginners, so email and ask what they provide before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm interested in learning more about the flipped classroom method.
reply: Rotate it head to foot every three months, and only flip it if the label or the shop says it is two-sided: most modern mattresses have their comfort layer on top and are made never to be turned over. A two-sided one gets flipped and rotated on the same schedule; a pillow-top or memory-foam one is only rotated, because flipping puts the soft layer underneath.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting ideas?
reply: Get something that shows you noticed: a book by an author they mentioned, a better version of something they use every day, or an afternoon planned around their favourite thing. The best gifts are specific to one person, so start from what they talk about.

instruction: I'm trying to get more into team sports. What are some popular options?
reply: Look for a club that advertises a beginners' or "back to" session rather than a team trials night — most sports now run them, and the standard is friendly. Try three in a month before you judge, and go twice before deciding you are unfit for it, because the first session is always the worst one.

instruction: I'm looking for eco-friendly cleaning products for my home. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: An eco wash is the long one, three and a half to four hours, because it heats the water slowly and soaks rather than blasts; the standard programme is about two hours and the quick one 30 to 60 minutes. Use eco for a full load and the quick wash for a light one, and skip the pre-rinse if you are running it the same day.

instruction: I was wondering, what happens when sound hits a wall?
reply: Sound goes through a wall more than people expect: earplugs and a heavy curtain or a bookcase against the shared wall take the edge off, and a fan or white noise masks the rest. If it is the room next door, ask them once at a calm time to turn it down after a set hour; if it keeps happening, keep a short log of the times and your council's noise team can act on it.

instruction: I'm having some trouble with my family. We always seem to be arguing about something.
reply: Say the one thing that stings most, once, as your own feeling rather than a verdict on them: 'When you say that about my job it makes me not want to ring.' If it is about your children, give the decision rather than the argument - 'we do bedtime this way, and it isn't up for debate every Sunday' - and give a short, boring answer to the rest.

instruction: I'm looking forward to the Olympic Games. What sports are featured in the Olympics?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm interested in theater direction. What is the role of a theater director?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about string instruments. What's the most popular one?
reply: Nine times in ten it is the strings: new ones stretch for a week, so tune up, bend every string a little, and tune again - three or four times the first evening. Old strings go dead and stop holding pitch, so if they are more than a few months old, change them.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately, so I was thinking about starting a dream journal to see if it helps me understand my sleep patterns better.
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: I'm trying to update my wardrobe, but I'm not sure how to incorporate the latest fashion trends into my personal style.
reply: Dress one step smarter than the job's everyday clothes on your first day: a shirt or blouse and smart trousers, a jacket if you own one, and closed clean shoes. Look at photos of the team or the office, and keep the trainers and hoodie for after you've seen what everyone else wears.

instruction: What is a web browser?
reply: A browser is the program you read websites in: Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox are the common four and they all do the same job. Anything you type in the address bar, any page you save a password for and any tab you leave open belongs to that one browser, which is why an account that works on your phone can look lost on a laptop until you sign in.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Italian cuisine. What's a popular Italian dish?
reply: One big dish that stretches beats several small ones: a chilli, a curry or a pasta bake with bread and a big salad, where the cheap starch and veg do the filling and the meat is the flavour. Chicken thighs, mince, tinned tomatoes, lentils and beans cost far less than prime cuts or fillets, and a slow-cooked shoulder of pork or lamb feeds a table for very little.

instruction: I'm interested in team sports. What are some popular team sports?
reply: Look for a club that advertises a beginners' or "back to" session rather than a team trials night — most sports now run them, and the standard is friendly. Try three in a month before you judge, and go twice before deciding you are unfit for it, because the first session is always the worst one.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding fractions. Can you explain what a fraction is?
reply: A fraction is a part of a whole written as one number over another: the bottom says how many equal pieces the whole is cut into and the top says how many of those you have, so 3/4 is three pieces out of four. The one thing that trips people up is that the same amount has lots of names - 2/4 is 1/2, and 0.5 is 1/2 too - which is why you can simplify and compare them by putting them over the same bottom number.

instruction: I'm concerned about water safety at home. What are some common hazards I should know about?
reply: One thing out of the house and one long thing at home is what saves a wet day. Out: the swimming pool, the library, a free museum gallery, or a walk in proper waterproofs, because a wet park is empty.

instruction: I'm planning to start going to the gym. What are some basic exercises I should do?
reply: For a first session you need very little: shorts or leggings that stretch, a t-shirt, trainers with a bit of support, a water bottle, a small towel and a padlock for the locker. That is the whole list - no gym turns anyone away for supermarket kit, and the machines are set up for exactly that.

instruction: I'm looking for information about French cuisine. What's a popular French dish?
reply: One big dish that stretches beats several small ones: a chilli, a curry or a pasta bake with bread and a big salad, where the cheap starch and veg do the filling and the meat is the flavour. Chicken thighs, mince, tinned tomatoes, lentils and beans cost far less than prime cuts or fillets, and a slow-cooked shoulder of pork or lamb feeds a table for very little.

instruction: I'm looking for an all-inclusive resort for my next vacation. What are some popular options?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you know what could be causing it?
reply: Sleep apnoea is the airway at the back of the throat closing for ten seconds or more, many times a night, so breathing stops in short bursts and you wake just enough to start again - which is why the snoring breaks off and why eight hours leaves you flat. The signs are loud snoring with silences, a gasp or a choke, a dry mouth and a morning headache, and nodding off in the day; extra weight, a thick neck, alcohol at night and sleeping on your back all make it worse.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Africa and I'm excited to see some wildlife. What are some common animals to see on a safari?
reply: In a British city park in winter you'll usually see robins, blackbirds, blue tits, great tits, pigeons, crows and magpies, with gulls and starlings on the grass. Look in the bushes and bare trees rather than the open lawn, and early morning is the busiest time.

instruction: I'm looking for a new car. What are some important safety features to consider?
reply: Only if the fault is not brakes, steering, a tyre or an overheating engine: those four need recovering, because a short drive can turn a cheap repair into a dangerous one, and a car with a 'dangerous' MOT fail must not be on the road at all. Anything else - a lamp, a wiper, an exhaust blow, a noisy bearing - can be driven to the garage or to a pre-booked test, slowly, with half an eye on the temperature gauge.

instruction: I'm looking for some fun activities to do with my family this weekend. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Do one thing you could not do with them in the house and one thing that is only rest, and put the fun one first, because the tidying can wait until Sunday evening. The first night can feel strange and quiet, and that is normal rather than a sign anything is wrong.

instruction: I'm looking to return a shirt I bought online, but I'm not sure about the store's return policy.
reply: Buying online gives you a 14-day right to change your mind from the day it arrives, and you only pay the return postage unless the shop says otherwise; buying in a shop gives you no right to change your mind at all, only the shop's own policy. That is the real difference, not the price.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New York City. What is the best way to get around the city?
reply: Plan the outing around the walking. Go door to door - a taxi, or the bus that stops nearest the door - and make a bench or a cafe the turning point so the trip is two short walks with a sit in between.

instruction: I love watching cooking shows. What's your favorite cooking show?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm looking for a gift for my sister's birthday. What kind of personalized gifts do you have?
reply: Make the gift something you do together: a picnic at the spot of your first date, a small photo book of the year, or a jar of twelve notes with one to open each month. The thought shows in the specifics, not the price.

instruction: I'm interested in smart clothing. What is it?
reply: For most interviews, smart casual is the safe bet: a clean shirt or blouse, dark trousers or a skirt, and closed shoes; a suit only if the company is formal. Check the office on their website or LinkedIn and dress one step smarter than that.

instruction: I'm looking for a taxi service that can accommodate my wheelchair. Do you know of any options?
reply: On a bus or a coach it travels folded, so have it down and the child out of it before the doors open: a driver can refuse a pushchair that is still open, and the space by the door belongs to a wheelchair user first. On trains and the underground a folded pushchair is free and goes in the luggage rack, and most stations have a lift, so use that rather than the escalator.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do you have any tips on how to improve my sleep quality?
reply: Stand up and move for two minutes every half hour, drink water, and put a bright light on your face — sleepiness at a desk is often boredom plus warm air. Do the hardest thing first and leave the reading for when you are flagging.

instruction: I'm looking for a new TV show to watch. What's a popular show right now?
reply: *The Rewatchables* is one film an episode and why it still works, which is the best listen for someone who likes films. *Kermode & Mayo's Take* reviews what is out now, and *You Must Remember This* tells the old Hollywood stories properly.

instruction: I'm having trouble meeting my deadlines at work. What are some common factors that affect job performance?
reply: Write down what is actually due this week, then pick three things a day and put them in the diary as blocks; the rest waits, and that is fine. Real deadlines go in first, the urgent-but-not-important jobs get one slot a day, and the way to protect the rest is to say no to one thing out loud.

instruction: I'm looking for a way to cook a tender pot roast. What's the best method?
reply: Set the oven to 150C (130C fan, gas 2) for a slow roast: lower than that and the meat sits in the danger zone for hours, higher and the outside dries before the middle softens. A covered pot keeps it moist, and a shoulder of lamb or pork or a beef brisket wants 4 to 5 hours.

instruction: My little brother swallowed some soap. What should I do?
reply: Cool running water now, and stay under it for twenty minutes: that is the part that limits the damage, and a cloth or a soap is not it. While the water runs, take off anything the chemical has soaked into - a sleeve, a watch, a ring.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get some exercise. Do you know any local walking groups I could join?
reply: Yes: it builds flexibility and balance and strengthens the muscles that hold you up, and it counts as exercise, though the heart and lungs get less from it than from a brisk walk. Two or three sessions a week is where the change shows, and a weekly class plus ten minutes at home most days is the usual way people keep it up.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm not sure what to feed her. What's a good type of cat food?
reply: Feed a kitten kitten food, not cat food, four small meals a day until about six months and then two: wet food plus a little dry suits most, and leave water out in a wide bowl. A kitten should gain weight steadily, so weigh her weekly and ask the vet if she does not.

instruction: It's going to be really hot today. What kind of clothes should I wear?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm thinking about my grandparents. What are some gift ideas for them?
reply: Make the gift something you do together: a picnic at the spot of your first date, a small photo book of the year, or a jar of twelve notes with one to open each month. The thought shows in the specifics, not the price.

instruction: What is the speed of sound?
reply: Sound is a vibration that travels as a wave through air, water or solids; in air it moves at about 343 metres per second. It travels faster in water and fastest in solids, and it cannot travel through a vacuum because there is nothing to vibrate.

instruction: I'm learning about the solar system in school. What is the biggest planet?
reply: Jupiter is the biggest planet: about 143,000 km across, or 11 Earths side by side, and more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together. It is a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.

instruction: I just bought a new wooden table, and I want to keep it looking nice. What's the best way to clean it?
reply: Scrub it with half a lemon and a big pinch of salt, rinse in the hottest water you have and dry it standing up: that lifts onion, garlic and fish out of wood or plastic. Plastic boards can go through the dishwasher, wooden ones should never.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into my gym routine, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: For a first session you need very little: shorts or leggings that stretch, a t-shirt, trainers with a bit of support, a water bottle, a small towel and a padlock for the locker. That is the whole list - no gym turns anyone away for supermarket kit, and the machines are set up for exactly that.

instruction: I'm learning about natural resources. What are some examples of natural resources found on Earth?
reply: A mineral is a natural solid with a definite chemical make-up and a crystal structure, formed in the earth without anything living making it: quartz, calcite and iron ore are minerals. A rock is usually a mixture of minerals.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about stars. What is the brightest star in the night sky?
reply: From a dark place you can see about 2,000 to 3,000 stars at once, and the whole sky holds around 9,000 visible to the naked eye. The Milky Way alone has 100 to 400 billion, and the observable universe has more stars than there are grains of sand on Earth.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game to play with friends. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: I'm planning to cook chicken for dinner. How do I handle it safely?
reply: Chicken is the one to be strict about: a sour or ammonia smell, a tacky or slimy feel, or any change of colour means bin it, and cooking it will not make it safe. Raw chicken keeps 1 to 2 days in the fridge and cooked chicken 3; if it has sat out warm for more than 2 hours, that is enough on its own.

instruction: I'm learning about the Earth's rock cycle in school. What is it?
reply: The rock cycle is rocks being made, broken down and made again. Magma cools to igneous rock such as granite or basalt; wind and water wear any rock into grains that settle, get squashed and cement into sedimentary rock such as limestone and sandstone; heat and pressure bake or squeeze rock into metamorphic rock such as marble, from limestone, or slate, from shale.

instruction: What is density?
reply: Density is how much mass is packed into a volume: a block of iron and a block of foam the same size have very different densities. Water has a density of about 1 kg per litre, which is why things less dense than water float.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with a difficult client. Do you have any tips?
reply: Treat it like a meeting, not a phone call: sit at a table with your notes, the job description and four stories written out in front of you - a week you organised, a difficult customer, something you fixed, a time you got it wrong and changed. Sit upright or stand, because the voice carries better.

instruction: I have a senior dog and I'm worried he's not getting enough exercise. What are some good exercises for older dogs?
reply: It's a hard thing to watch, and being scared for him is part of loving an old dog. What helps most is a vet check now and every six months: pain relief for stiff joints, a senior food, and a plan for the bad days.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I want to compare prices before I buy one. Do you know any good websites for that?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm looking for a carpool to work. Can you help me find one?
reply: Not for the small jobs: a dripping tap, a loo that keeps running, a blocked trap, a ball valve or a washing-machine hose is an hour with a spanner and a few pounds in parts. Call one when the water will not stop at the stopcock, the leak is under a floor or inside a wall, a joint still weeps after two goes, or the job is a new bathroom or a boiler swap.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping lately. I'm 60 years old. Do you think my age has something to do with it?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm thinking of installing a smart security system in my home. What are some popular options?
reply: A smart plug goes between the socket and the thing, and you switch it from an app or by voice; it is the cheapest way to make a lamp, a fan or a Christmas tree smart. Check it is rated for what you plug in (13A for a heater, and never for anything that must not be cut off, like an iron or an electric blanket) and that it works with what you already have, Alexa or Google or Apple Home.

instruction: I love watching cooking shows. What are some popular reality cooking shows?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I have a small plant and I was wondering if it needs light.
reply: Plants need sunlight as the energy source for photosynthesis, the reaction that makes their food. Without enough light they cannot make sugar, so they stop growing and their leaves yellow and drop.

instruction: I'm feeling stuck in my 9-to-5 job. What's the typical work schedule for most office jobs?
reply: Give the day a shape: same start time, dressed, a real lunch away from the desk, and a walk to end it. Put the phone in another room for one 50-minute block before you open email, and have one call with a colleague a day - the office is what you are missing, so put a bit of it back in the week.

instruction: I was wondering, what happens to plants during winter?
reply: The garden in winter is mostly tidying and waiting: clear the dead stems but leave seed heads and any hollow stalks standing, because insects shelter in them and the birds eat the seeds. Mulch bare soil with compost or bark, but only once the ground is not frozen, and stay off wet or frozen grass because footprints kill the blades under them.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What's a simple machine?
reply: *Codenames* (2 minutes to learn, works with any group), *Ticket to Ride* (simple, satisfying trains) and *Sushi Go!* (fast, small, cheap) are the three to start with. All are done in under an hour.

instruction: I'm looking for a scenic train route for my next vacation. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Pick a route you already know on quiet streets, ride it once at a weekend so the turns are not a surprise, and start with two days a week rather than five. Leave a lock, a spare tube and a pair of shoes at work, so there is nothing to carry and nothing to forget.

instruction: I'm wondering about the different types of rainfall. What are some main types?
reply: Precipitation is water falling out of the sky - rain, snow, sleet or hail - when droplets in a cloud join up until they are too heavy to stay up. It is one step of the water cycle, after evaporation and condensation.

instruction: I was wondering, how do animals communicate with each other using sound?
reply: Sound is a pressure wave travelling through air, water or a solid: something vibrates, pushes the particles next to it, and the push travels outwards. It cannot cross a vacuum, and it goes faster through water and solids than through air.

instruction: I'm planning to start running. What are the basic things I need to get started?
reply: Start with run-walk: three minutes of easy running, two minutes of walking, five times, three days a week, and add a minute of running each week. Build up for six weeks before you add speed, keep every run slow enough to talk, and expect the first fortnight to feel harder than it looks.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm worried she's getting bored. What can I do to keep her entertained?
reply: Cats chew plastic and string for the crinkle and the texture, and it is usually boredom or hunting that has nowhere to go: a wand-toy game before meals, a cardboard box to shred and a chew-safe toy give her something better to do. Keep bags, rubber bands, hair ties, tinsel and string out of reach, because a cat that swallows them can get a linear blockage that needs surgery.

instruction: I'm learning about the life cycle of frogs. What is the first stage?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm interested in wearable displays. What are some common types?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I need to measure the length of my room, but I don't have a tape measure. Is there a way to estimate it?
reply: Area is the amount of surface inside a shape, measured in square units: a room 4 m by 3 m has an area of 12 square metres. For a rectangle it is length times width, for a triangle half base times height, and for a circle pi times the radius squared.

instruction: I'm going on a trip next week and I need help with packing. Can you tell me what I should bring?
reply: Pack what you use least first - books, spare bedding, the cupboard under the stairs - and keep a 'first night' box out of the van: kettle, mugs, chargers, loo roll, bedding and a change of clothes. Label boxes by room, do one room an evening for the last three weeks, and get rid of anything you have not touched in a year rather than paying to move it.

instruction: I'm a huge fan of live concerts. What's the best way to find out about upcoming concerts in my area?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I want to increase my flexibility. What are some good exercises?
reply: Pilates is the better pick for a weak or sore back and a strong middle - it is slow, controlled work on the deep stomach and hip muscles - and yoga is the better pick for flexibility, balance and winding down. Both are low-impact and fine to start from nothing, so if the choice is still even, take the one whose teacher you liked.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm worried about her health. What are some common signs of illness in cats?
reply: Chronic kidney disease is the kidneys slowly losing their filtering over months to years: it is the commonest long illness of an older cat, it is found on bloods rather than by looking, and most cats found early live for years with it. A prescription renal diet - wet food lower in phosphate and protein - is the one thing shown to slow it, and any wet food she will eat beats dry.

instruction: I'm a huge fan of concerts. What's it like backstage at a concert?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm having trouble with basic addition. Can you help me?
reply: Work in this order: brackets, then powers or roots, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right. So 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, not 20.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do you know anything about restless leg syndrome?
reply: Restless legs feel like a crawl or a fizz in the legs in the evening that only moving eases. Ask a GP for a blood test first, because low iron is a common cause; cut caffeine and alcohol late, and try a warm bath and calf stretches before bed.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I'm not sure which brand to choose. What's the difference between Dell and HP?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm looking for online learning platforms. Have you heard of Khan Academy?
reply: Both are state schools and free to attend. A maintained school is run by the local authority; an academy is funded directly by the government, sets its own curriculum and admissions, and is run by a trust.

instruction: I'm looking for a new video camera for my YouTube channel. What type of camera is best for recording videos?
reply: Look for the dot at the top of the screen: green means the camera is on, orange means the microphone, and it only appears while an app is using it. If it shows when you are not in any app, open Settings > Privacy > Camera (Permissions on Android, Privacy & security on a laptop) and turn off every app you do not trust, then restart the phone; a camera nobody can account for is worth a backup and a factory reset rather than a new phone.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure how to pack lightly. Do you have any tips for minimalist packing?
reply: Pack what you use least first - books, spare bedding, the cupboard under the stairs - and keep a 'first night' box out of the van: kettle, mugs, chargers, loo roll, bedding and a change of clothes. Label boxes by room, do one room an evening for the last three weeks, and get rid of anything you have not touched in a year rather than paying to move it.

instruction: I'm new to weightlifting at the gym. What is spotting in weightlifting?
reply: Add weight when you can hit the top of your rep range on every set with clean form - usually every week or two when you are new. Take the smallest jump you have, 2.5kg on a bar or the next dumbbell up, and expect to lose a rep or two for a session or so; that is the new weight working, not a bad day.

instruction: I have allergies and I'm wondering what season is usually the worst for allergies.
reply: A sneeze is the nose throwing out something that irritates its lining, and what helps depends on which of the two usual causes it is. If your eyes or the roof of your mouth itch, it is an allergy: a once-a-day antihistamine started before you go out, a saline rinse, windows shut in pollen season and a shower before bed.

instruction: I'm looking for information about vintage clothing. What's the most popular type of vintage clothing?
reply: Familiar, subdued clothes are the thing: black or dark colours, smart and comfortable, and nothing new needed. If the family asked for bright colours or a football shirt, follow that instead, because it's about them.

instruction: I want to cook something simple in the microwave. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Pasta cooks fine in a microwave, in a big bowl with plenty of room: cover it with boiling water from the kettle, add a good pinch of salt, and give it 8 to 10 minutes on full power, stirring once at the halfway point so the pieces at the top get turned under. Use a bowl at least twice the size of the pasta, because it foams up over the edge otherwise.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics in school, and I was wondering, what's the difference between genes and environment when it comes to how we look and behave?
reply: A gene is a section of DNA that holds the instructions for making one thing the body needs, usually a protein: eye colour, blood type and how a muscle works all come from genes. You inherit half your genes from each parent, and they switch on and off depending on the cell.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. Is it true that the sea level is rising?
reply: A sea breeze is the cool air blowing in off the sea on a sunny afternoon, because land heats faster than water, so the warm air over the land rises and the cooler sea air moves in to replace it. At night the pattern reverses as the land cools faster.

instruction: I'm looking for a new webcam for video calls. What's a good brand?
reply: For essays, video calls and Netflix, almost anything current works: 8GB RAM, a 256GB SSD and a 14 inch screen, around £400 to £550. A Chromebook is fine if everything lives in Google Docs, but avoid it for a course that needs Windows software.

instruction: I'm trying to save energy at home. What are some ways to do that?
reply: Energy comes from sleep, daylight and food, in that order: the same bedtime and getting-up time every day, ten minutes outside in the morning light, and a lunch with protein and slow carbs rather than just a sandwich, so three o'clock does not flatten you. Water through the day and no caffeine after two help too.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. I enjoy cooking and trying new recipes.
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: What is a hammer used for?
reply: Turn the hammer off and use a tile bit, or an ordinary masonry bit with the drill on rotary only: the hammer is what cracks the glaze, and porcelain wants a proper spear-point bit. Put a square of masking tape over the spot so the bit cannot skate, mark the hole through it, and start at a low speed and a shallow angle with almost no pressure until the glaze is through, then straighten up and keep a wet sponge or a squirt of water on the bit because the heat is the other thing that splits a tile.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different types of food. What's your favorite type of cuisine?
reply: Cheese, chutney and an apple; cream cheese with smoked salmon or cucumber; hummus and something crunchy; butter and a sliced boiled egg with salt and pepper. Anything soft wants something crisp on it, and anything dry wants something wet.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to stay healthy at work. What's the most important thing to do?
reply: Treat it as a work problem with a health cost, and act on both: tell your GP how it is affecting sleep, eating and mood, because a sick note and a few weeks off are normal and protect your job. At work, ask for the specific change that would help - fewer shifts, a different manager, a written plan - since adjustments are easier to say yes to than "less stress".

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise routine and I've heard about HIIT. What is it?
reply: A hiccup is a sudden spasm of the diaphragm followed by your vocal cords snapping shut, which makes the 'hic' sound. It usually happens after a big meal, a fizzy drink or a laugh, when the stomach pushes up against the diaphragm, and it is harmless.

instruction: I'm a high school student and I'm having trouble choosing between French and Spanish for my foreign language class. What's the difference?
reply: Pick by what you will actually use it for, not by which is easiest on paper: the language of the country you visit, or of the family you are marrying into, beats any ranking. With no reason to choose, Spanish is the usual bet - about 500 million speakers, spelling that matches the sound, and a lot of cheap material - and if you already have French or Italian, the other one of the pair is the cheapest start of all.

instruction: I'm looking for some new window treatments for my living room. What are some popular options?
reply: Cool the room before you get in, not after: windows open and a fan on for half an hour, then a lukewarm shower and dry off properly. Cotton sheets, one light layer rather than a duvet, and a damp flannel on your neck or feet.

instruction: I'm looking for advice on finding a mentor at work. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Say yes to everything small for the first month - lunch, a coffee, the drink after work - because that is where the friendships actually happen, and nobody notices who said yes. Ask people about their own work rather than talking about yours: "how long have you been doing this?" and "what is the bit nobody warns you about?" get real answers.

instruction: I'm interested in ancient civilizations. Can you tell me about the Egyptians?
reply: Ancient Egyptians built them about 4,500 years ago, around 2560 BC for the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu. The workers were organised, paid labourers, not slaves, hauling stone on ramps and sledges.

instruction: I'm looking for a new game to play. What are some popular games right now?
reply: *Patchwork*, *Jaipur* and *Hive* are the three best two-player games that are quick to learn. For a card game with no kit, gin rummy works just fine.

instruction: I'm interested in wearable health monitoring devices. What's the most popular one?
reply: For the gym: trainers you only wear indoors, two towels (one for the floor and machines), a water bottle, a padlock for the locker, deodorant and a bag for wet kit. A resistance band and a notebook beat anything else a shop will sell you.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and overwhelmed. What are some ways to relax?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What is melatonin?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm having some trouble with my family. We don't seem to communicate very well.
reply: Ask once, in your own words, and make it about them rather than a list of charges: 'You seem a bit off with me - have I done something?' Then leave room for the answer. If they say nothing is wrong, take it at face value and carry on as normal; most of the time it is their week and not you, and a second and third 'are you okay?' is what makes it awkward.

instruction: I have a new puppy at home, and I'm having trouble with house training.
reply: Meet on neutral ground, one walker each, and walk them side by side rather than face to face, then let them off lead only in a fenced space where the older dog can walk away. At home give the older dog his own bed, bowl and corner that the puppy cannot reach, feed them apart, and step in before the puppy hangs off his ears.

instruction: I'm planning my sister's birthday party and I was wondering about some family traditions for birthdays.
reply: Ask the host what the dress code is, then dress for the kind of party: jeans and a nice top for a house party, something dressier for a bar or a big birthday. Wear the shoes you can stand in for four hours, and a layer that survives a warm room.

instruction: I'm looking for a last-minute gift for my sister's birthday. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Make the gift something you do together: a picnic at the spot of your first date, a small photo book of the year, or a jar of twelve notes with one to open each month. The thought shows in the specifics, not the price.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is it?
reply: The rock cycle is rocks being made, broken down and made again. Magma cools to igneous rock such as granite or basalt; wind and water wear any rock into grains that settle, get squashed and cement into sedimentary rock such as limestone and sandstone; heat and pressure bake or squeeze rock into metamorphic rock such as marble, from limestone, or slate, from shale.

instruction: I'm going shopping for some new clothes this weekend. What's a good accessory to add to an outfit?
reply: Buy one pair of dark trousers in the size that fits you now and one plain shirt, this week rather than on the morning: those two do more for how you look than an expensive jacket that does not button. Ask for the trousers to be taken up while you are in the shop.

instruction: What's on TV tonight?
reply: I can't see tonight's listings, so here is what I would start instead: *Happy Valley* if you want tense, *The Detectorists* if you want gentle, or *Groundhog Day* if you want a film you can rely on. Tell me the mood and I'll narrow it.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my dog barking nonstop. Do you have any advice?
reply: A growl is a warning rather than a fault, so the first thing is to stop what you were doing, step back and let him come to you - and never tell a dog off for growling, because a dog punished for the warning learns to skip it and go straight to the snap. Then find out what it is about: being picked up or handled, a hand near his food, bed or a stolen sock, or pain.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What do you think about photography?
reply: Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I'm looking for a job in retail. What are some common job categories?
reply: Look for the places that sell a lot of one thing: a market hall or a food court, a bakery, a cafe at the back of a shop, a street food van in a regular spot, or the lunch board outside a restaurant that wants the office trade. Walk a street back from the station or the main road, where the rents are lower, and follow the queue of people who work nearby.

instruction: I'm thinking about walking to work instead of driving. What are some benefits of walking to work?
reply: Yes: it builds flexibility and balance and strengthens the muscles that hold you up, and it counts as exercise, though the heart and lungs get less from it than from a brisk walk. Two or three sessions a week is where the change shows, and a weekly class plus ten minutes at home most days is the usual way people keep it up.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What are some things that can help me fall asleep faster?
reply: Give yourself a run-up rather than trying to switch off: the same wake-up time every day, no caffeine after about two, the last hour dim with the phone out of reach, and a cool dark room. Falling asleep is a slope you slide down, so nothing you try harder at helps: if you are still awake after about twenty minutes, get up, sit somewhere dim with something dull, and go back when your eyes are heavy.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Africa for wildlife photography. What's the best time to visit?
reply: Agree the length before you go, in the same breath as the date: two nights is plenty for most trips, and a day trip leaves you both glad to have seen each other. Take something for the table rather than a present, and book the way home before you arrive so the last hour is not the anxious one.

instruction: I'm looking for a place to eat with my family. What types of restaurants are good for families?
reply: A corner shop covers more of a dinner than people expect: rice, pasta, eggs, tinned beans and chickpeas, tinned tomatoes, frozen peas, onions, potatoes, milk, cheese and a curry powder or stock cubes. What it will not have is fresh herbs, good bread or anything unusual, so take the dried or tinned version rather than going without.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the countryside next week, and I'm worried about the rain. Does rain affect agriculture?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm looking for a city break in Europe. What are some popular destinations?
reply: Berlin has about 3.8 million people, the biggest city in Germany and about eight times the size of Frankfurt.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about subway expansion projects in my city. Are there any new lines being built?
reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Costa Rica and I'm looking for eco-lodges. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: A tent and bags for everyone, plus what small children need on a campsite: a mat each, because they feel every root, warm layers and a hat for the night even in July, and a full change of clothes kept in the car so a wet sleeping bag is not the end of the trip. Take a torch each, wet wipes, a bin bag for wet things, breakfast that needs no cooking, and something to do after dark.

instruction: I'm painting my room and I'm trying to decide on a color. What's a good color for a bedroom?
reply: Matt white, or the palest tint of the wall colour, and one shade lighter than the walls if you want a tint at all: a ceiling painted as deep as the walls comes down on you and makes a small room feel lower. White bounces light back into the room, which is why a dark hallway or a north-facing room looks better with a warm white than a cool one, and a sunlit south room can take a cool white.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites for educational videos?
reply: Match the limit to the age: under two, video calls and the odd photo only; two to five, an hour of good programmes a day; older children, a set amount agreed in advance. Watch it with them when you can, keep screens away from meals and the hour before bed, and have one screen-free part of each day so it isn't a fight every time.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something sporty. What sports are easy to learn?
reply: Search for the sport plus your town and 'club', then email and ask about a taster session: most clubs have a beginners' or social night that costs a few pounds. Turn up to that rather than a match, and say you're new — clubs are used to it, and it's the fastest way to find people at your level.

instruction: I'm planning to organize my home. Can you tell me about the laundry room?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm going on a beach vacation next week and I'm not sure what to pack.
reply: For a week: five tops, three bottoms, two layers, one pair of shoes you can walk in and one smarter pair, plus a waterproof, swimwear if there is water, chargers and any tickets. Plan to wash once on day three or four - a hostel or a launderette - and you can halve the clothes.

instruction: I'm planning a ski trip and I'm worried there won't be enough snow. Do ski resorts make their own snow?
reply: Snow forms when water vapour freezes straight into ice crystals high in a cloud, and the crystals stick together as they fall. It only reaches the ground as snow if the air stays cold all the way down, which is why a cold snap often brings sleet instead.

instruction: I'm looking for information about celebrity fashion lines. Can you tell me about some popular ones?
reply: For most interviews, smart casual is the safe bet: a clean shirt or blouse, dark trousers or a skirt, and closed shoes; a suit only if the company is formal. Check the office on their website or LinkedIn and dress one step smarter than that.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm interested in educational travel. What are some places I should visit?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm a bit worried about climate change. Is it really happening?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

reply: Natural selection is how evolution works: individuals vary, the ones whose variations suit their surroundings have more surviving young, and those variations become common over generations. It is not a plan or a choice - the environment simply filters what is already there.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. What are some common sleep disorders?
reply: Sleep talking is common and almost always harmless: it happens in light sleep, it runs in families, and most people never know they do it. Nothing needs treating - keep the last drink early, cut late caffeine and get enough sleep, because it gets worse when someone is overtired or feverish.

instruction: I have a brother and a sister, and we always fight. Is that normal?
reply: A grown sibling's jealousy is usually about one visible difference - a house, a partner, a job, or the way a parent treats you - so do not defend your life or list your own hard parts, which reads as scoring points. Name it once, plainly and without blame: 'I know this has not been easy to watch.' Then keep the relationship on ground that is not a comparison, and if every visit turns into digs or competition, make them shorter and more structured.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my home safer. What are some common home security systems?
reply: Put the key in one place that you walk past on the way out - a hook inside the front door - and nowhere else, because the pockets, the bag and the coat are what lose it. A spare with a neighbour or family is free and saves the locksmith, and a key safe by the door (about twenty pounds, screwed on, with a code) covers the rest.

instruction: I'm looking for a weekend getaway from New York City. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick a route you already know on quiet streets, ride it once at a weekend so the turns are not a surprise, and start with two days a week rather than five. Leave a lock, a spare tube and a pair of shoes at work, so there is nothing to carry and nothing to forget.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, but I'm not sure what type of work I want to do. What are some common job categories?

Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my daily commute easier. I've heard of park and ride options, but I'm not sure how they work.
reply: Worth it if the alternative is driving: a pedal-assist bike flattens the hills and the headwind, so a commute you would skip on a bad day still happens, for a few pence of electricity a charge and no tax or parking. It saves little against a bus pass and keeps you less fit unless you turn the assist down.

instruction: I'm a farmer and I'm worried about the wind affecting my crops. How does wind affect agriculture?
reply: Wind is air moving from an area of high pressure to one of low pressure, and the sun creates those differences by heating land and sea unevenly. The bigger the pressure gap, the stronger the wind.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping and I'm looking for organic products. What's the difference between organic and non-organic?
reply: It means you don't like it much, said politely. What is it that isn't for you?

instruction: I'm having trouble reading my textbooks for school. Do you have any tips?
reply: Find the first topic you stopped understanding rather than the newest one, because everything after it is built on it: go through the textbook contents or the topic list and mark the last thing that made sense. Then do three things - tell the teacher you have fallen behind and ask which two topics matter most for the next test, spend twenty minutes a day on those two only, and get one session with a classmate who is good at them.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school and I'm a bit confused. Can you tell me what a force is?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed with work and struggling to find a balance. Do you have any tips for work-life balance?

instruction: I'm a parent and I'm looking for information about the upcoming school play. Do you have any details?
reply: Ask other parents at the school gate first: a sitter vouched for by someone you know beats any app. Then do one evening while you are still in the house, paying them to play while you get on with something, so the first real night out isn't the first time.

instruction: I'm thirsty, what are some popular juice options?
reply: If you are drinking far more than usual and still thirsty, see a GP: thirst that will not quench is worth a blood test, because it can be the first sign of diabetes. If it is just habit, spread the day's drinks out, keep water out of sight between meals, and sip rather than down a pint at once - but do not ration it, since your body asks for what it needs.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering what an atom is.
reply: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, with a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons. Atoms join into molecules, and everything you can touch is made of them; they are mostly empty space.

instruction: I'm hungry, what's a good breakfast food?
reply: Breakfast is not magic, and skipping it does not make you fat or thin on its own: what matters is the total day. If you are hungry in the morning, eat something with protein and fibre - eggs, porridge, yoghurt and fruit - because it makes the mid-morning biscuit much less likely.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to preserve my family's recipes. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: A rug, a cool bag with a freezer block, plates and cups you do not mind losing, a bottle opener, napkins, a bin bag and water. Skip anything heavy with mayonnaise unless it is eaten within the hour: sausage rolls, cheese, fruit and a flask keep for hours.

reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I was wondering, where does the word "quarantine" come from?
reply: A guarantor is someone who signs to pay if you stop paying, so they are on the hook for the whole rent or loan, not just a month of it. Letting agents ask for one when your income is under about 30 times the monthly rent.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, what are some popular workplace environments?
reply: Split your week in half: five tailored applications, and three conversations with people who might know someone. Most jobs come through a person rather than a portal, so tell ten people you trust exactly what you are looking for.

instruction: I'm looking for a new purse. What are some popular types of handbags right now?
reply: An airbag is a cloth bag that a chemical charge fills with nitrogen in about a twentieth of a second: a sensor spots the sudden stop and fires it, then it deflates so you can get out. It only works with the belt, the strap that locks when a sprung weight catches on a ratchet.

instruction: I'm looking for online courses to learn new skills, do you know about FutureLearn?
reply: Last-minute learning works for facts and structures, not skills: take the syllabus or mark scheme, list what is actually examinable, and learn the highest-mark items with self-testing. Sleep before the exam and skip the things you already know.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes to wear at home. What's a good option?
reply: Something comfortable and a step nicer than you'd wear at home: jeans with a good top, or a dress with flat shoes. Nothing that needs careful handling next to red wine on someone's sofa.

instruction: What are the main types of computers?
reply: A laptop if you will be typing - email, essays, spreadsheets, work - and a tablet if it is mostly reading, video, calls and games on the sofa. instruction: I'm feeling tired at work. What are some good break activities?
reply: Stand up and move for two minutes every half hour, drink water, and put a bright light on your face — sleepiness at a desk is often boredom plus warm air. Do the hardest thing first and leave the reading for when you are flagging.

instruction: I'm going shopping this weekend and I want to save some money. Do you have any tips on finding discounts?
reply: Start absurdly small if that's all there is: £5 a week by standing order on payday. Then find the money in the bills, a fresh energy comparison, a cheaper mobile or broadband contract and the subscriptions you forgot about usually free up £20 to £50 a month, and add whatever they save you.

instruction: I'm having trouble staying organized with my schoolwork. Do you have any tips for managing my homework?
reply: Write down what you actually see, with examples and dates - the meltdown at the same time each morning, the shoes he cannot bear, how long homework takes - because a pattern on paper is what gets taken seriously. instruction: I'm looking for a new word processing software. What are some popular options?
reply: Anything without words works best for focus: lo-fi hip hop, film scores by Hans Zimmer or Ólafur Arnalds, or ambient Brian Eno. Words compete with reading in a way that instrumentals don't.

What it will not have is fresh herbs, good bread or anything unusual, so take the dried or tinned version rather than going without.

instruction: I'm having trouble managing my homework. Do you have any tips?
reply: Homework earns its place in small doses: about ten minutes a night in the first years of primary, half an hour by the end of it and an hour or so at secondary, and the evidence for it is weakest for the youngest children. What makes it work is the same each night - a fixed time, a clear table, and you nearby without taking over.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Europe and I'm trying to decide on an airline. What are the main airline alliances?
reply: Be flexible on dates and airports and book eight to six weeks ahead for Europe, longer for long-haul. Tuesday and Wednesday flights are usually cheapest, and luggage fees often close the gap between budget and full-service airlines.

instruction: I'm planning to create a garden in my backyard, but I don't know where to start.
reply: Tidy the outline first, because a garden reads as untidy at its edges before its middle: cut the lawn edge right round with a half-moon edger, clear the path, and weed the first foot of border. Then buy three plants and no more - something tall, something scented by the door, and something that flowers for months - in pots if the soil is poor.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about Rugby. Is it a popular sport?
reply: In rugby's Six Nations, the Triple Crown goes to whichever of England, Ireland, Scotland or Wales beats the other three in the same season. In US horse racing it is winning the Kentucky Derby, the Preakness and the Belmont Stakes in one year.

instruction: I'm interested in cycling races. What are some popular types?
reply: It is about three weeks and 21 stages, and the winner is whoever finishes with the lowest total time — not the most stage wins. The yellow jersey goes to the overall leader each day, green is the points competition for sprinters, and the polka dot is for the best climber.

instruction: I'm planning a group trip to Paris with my friends. Can you tell me what time of year is best to visit?
reply: Agree the length before you go, in the same breath as the date: two nights is plenty for most trips, and a day trip leaves you both glad to have seen each other. Take something for the table rather than a present, and book the way home before you arrive so the last hour is not the anxious one.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family. What is family?
reply: For a family with an older parent, WhatsApp is the easiest: install it, add the contacts, then tap New group, name it and pick the people. Turn on their notifications for that one chat and pin it to the top of their screen, and start by sending a photo so there is something to reply to.

instruction: I'm learning about figure skating jumps. What's the difference between a toe loop and a loop jump?
reply: Both feet stay on the ground behind the line, and the ball goes back over your head with both hands on it from behind - a foot over the line or a hand that comes round the side turns it over. Plant both feet shoulder width, get some bend in the elbows and throw it flat to a teammate's feet rather than high and looping.

instruction: I was thinking about my family. I have two siblings. Do you know anything about siblings?
reply: A grown sibling's jealousy is usually about one visible difference - a house, a partner, a job, or the way a parent treats you - so do not defend your life or list your own hard parts, which reads as scoring points. Name it once, plainly and without blame: 'I know this has not been easy to watch.' Then keep the relationship on ground that is not a comparison, and if every visit turns into digs or competition, make them shorter and more structured.

instruction: How often should I wash my clothes?
reply: For a week: five tops, three bottoms, two layers, one pair of shoes you can walk in and one smarter pair, plus a waterproof, swimwear if there is water, chargers and any tickets. Plan to wash once on day three or four - a hostel or a launderette - and you can halve the clothes.

instruction: I'm having some issues with one of our vendors, they're not meeting their deadlines and it's affecting our project timeline.
reply: At the first meeting, split the work in writing with names and dates, and pick one person to hold the whole thing together. Swap drafts before the deadline so no one is the bottleneck.

instruction: I'm looking for a new TV show to binge-watch. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: I'm thinking of upgrading my home with some smart devices. What's the benefit of smart lighting?
reply: A smart plug goes between the socket and the thing, and you switch it from an app or by voice; it is the cheapest way to make a lamp, a fan or a Christmas tree smart. Check it is rated for what you plug in (13A for a heater, and never for anything that must not be cut off, like an iron or an electric blanket) and that it works with what you already have, Alexa or Google or Apple Home.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my work schedule. Can I work remotely?
reply: Give the day a hard edge and keep it the same one: laptop shut and work phone in a drawer at a fixed time, then something physical - a walk, a shower, cooking - because the body changes gear more reliably than the mind. Tell your team the hours once, in writing: "I'm offline after 6 and I pick up messages at 9." If you work from the room you live in, put the laptop out of sight at the end of the day; a screen in the corner is a shift that never ends.

instruction: I'm going to the airport tomorrow. What is air traffic control?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I've been getting sick a lot lately and I want to know how to boost my immune system.
reply: Adults get two to four colds a year, and they cluster when you are short of sleep, stressed or run down - that is not a weak immune system, it is the usual pattern. Sleep seven to nine hours, eat properly, wash your hands and take vitamin D in winter; see a GP if you are getting infections that need antibiotics more than a few times a year.

instruction: I'm having trouble remembering some formulas for my math test. Do you know any good ways to remember them?
reply: Ask in person after class with one specific thing ("I get the formula but I can't do the last question on the sheet"), and say what you've already tried. Teachers help far more often than students expect, and an email the same day saying thank you makes them remember you next time.

instruction: I'm planning to visit an amusement park this weekend and I want to know if you can help me navigate the park.
reply: Plan the outing around the walking. Go door to door - a taxi, or the bus that stops nearest the door - and make a bench or a cafe the turning point so the trip is two short walks with a sit in between.

instruction: I'm looking for a new cutting board. What are the different types?
reply: A mandoline is a flat board with a blade set at an adjustable height, for slices of even thickness - 2mm potato for dauphinoise, cabbage for slaw - which a knife cannot match for speed. It is also the sharpest thing in most kitchens: use the hand guard, or a cut glove, every time, and stop while there is still a knuckle's width of vegetable left.

instruction: I'm interested in photography as a hobby. What kind of camera should I get?
reply: Close every other app that might be holding the camera, then check the permission: on Windows, Settings > Privacy & security > Camera, and on a Mac, System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera, and switch your app on. A laptop with a sliding shutter over the lens is the other common one.

instruction: I have two siblings, an older brother and a younger sister. What's the birth order in my family?
reply: Expect it, name it, and do not argue them out of it: "it's hard having someone new in the house" lands better than "you love your sister really". Give the older one ten minutes a day that belong to nobody else, let them help with the baby only if they offer to, and blame the baby for nothing they can hear - "the baby needs me" rather than "you'll have to wait".

instruction: I'm going to the airport and I need a taxi. How much does a taxi ride to the airport usually cost?
reply: Book the bag with the ticket rather than at the airport: a checked bag is usually about £15 to £40 each way online and £40 to £65 at the desk, and on a short trip a 10 kg cabin bag with priority is often the cheaper way to take a case. Weigh it at home on the bathroom scales - a few kilos over is charged at the airport rate however you booked.

instruction: I'm looking for a new suit for a wedding, do you know anything about custom tailoring?
reply: Start from the invitation: the dress code, the time and the venue settle nearly all of it, because a 2pm church wedding and a 6pm hotel one want different clothes. With no code, go one step up from your smartest everyday outfit - a mid-length dress or a tailored trouser suit in a dark or jewel colour, closed shoes that cope with grass, and a layer for the evening.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about space. What's the brightest star in the sky?
reply: Space looks black because there is almost nothing there to scatter light into your eyes; light only reaches you if it comes straight from a star or a lit object. The sky is bright blue from Earth because our air scatters sunlight everywhere.

instruction: I'm looking for information about my local government. What are the main responsibilities of my city council?
reply: Your council is the layer below parliament, and it is usually two layers: a district or unitary council for bins, housing, planning permission and licensing, and a county council for schools, social care, libraries and most roads. It is paid for by council tax plus business rates and grants, and the councillors are elected locally every four years.

instruction: I want to learn about roasting vegetables in the oven. What temperature should I use?
reply: Cut vegetables into similar-sized pieces, toss them with oil and salt and roast at 200C (180C fan) for 30 to 40 minutes, turning once. Give them space on the tray; a crowded tray steams instead of roasting.

instruction: I'm thinking of replacing the flooring in my living room. What are some popular options?
reply: Pick the thing you cannot change - the floor, the tiles, the worktop, the sofa - and take the wall colour out of it in a paler version of itself. Then add one deeper tone from the same family for a rug or cushions and a wood or a metal to warm it: three colours, one of them a near-neutral.

instruction: I'm trying to find the next number in the pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Can you help me?
reply: Divide the top and the bottom by the same number until nothing goes into both: 6/8 divides by 2 to give 3/4, and that is as far as it goes. The number to start with is the highest common factor of the two.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night because of the noise in my neighborhood. What can I do to block out the noise?
reply: A steady sound is easier on sleep than a screen, because there's nothing to watch. Keep the radio or podcast low and on a sleep timer; if it is a fan or white noise, point it away from your face.

instruction: I'm looking for educational apps for my kids. Can you suggest some?
reply: Ask other parents at the school gate first: a sitter vouched for by someone you know beats any app. Then do one evening while you are still in the house, paying them to play while you get on with something, so the first real night out isn't the first time.

instruction: I'm looking for information about musical instruments. What is a violin?
reply: That is what headphones, a mute or a practice room are for, and most of it is cheaper than a row: a headphone amp for an electric guitar, a soundhole cover or a folded cloth in an acoustic, a practice mute for a violin or a brass instrument, and headphones on a digital piano. Pick the hours you would want quiet in yourself - not before nine and not after ten - and tell them once, cheerfully, that you play and when you stop.

instruction: What season is it right now?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm planning a trip with my family and we're thinking of visiting an amusement park. What are some popular amusement parks in the US?
reply: Plan the outing around the walking. Go door to door - a taxi, or the bus that stops nearest the door - and make a bench or a cafe the turning point so the trip is two short walks with a sit in between.

instruction: I'm looking for a new music streaming app. What are some popular options?
reply: In the Clock app, edit the alarm and tap Sound (iPhone) or the bell icon (Android) - on an iPhone the list ends with Pick a Song, which uses anything in your library, and on Android there is usually a plus sign to add a file. Start quiet and put the phone across the room: a gentle sound you have to get up to stop wakes you better than a loud one by the bed.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed lately and I want to start a self-care routine. What are some good activities for relaxation?
reply: The routine matters less than the regularity: same time, lights down, screens off, and something calm for the last half hour, like a shower, a few pages of a book or the dishes. Keep the bed for sleeping, and if you are not asleep in 20 minutes get up and read somewhere dim until you are sleepy.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my small apartment and I don't know where to start.
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm looking for information about food festivals. Are there any happening soon?
reply: Arrive early, when it is easier to join a small group, and ask people about the thing you are both already at: how they know the host, what they thought of the food. Have three open questions ready and let the other person do most of the talking.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a bike to ride to work. Are there any specific laws I should know about?
reply: The Cycle to Work scheme lets your employer buy a bike and safety kit - usually up to £1,000, and some employers set a higher limit - and take the cost out of your pay before tax, so a £1,000 bike costs a basic-rate taxpayer around £680. You pay it over 12 months as a hire fee, then either hand the bike back, pay a small final payment or keep it by extending the hire.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow, and I'm not sure what to expect.
reply: Book the check-up and say on the phone that you are nervous and have not been for a while - practices hear it every week, and most will give you a longer first appointment, a signal to stop, and no lecture. The first visit is usually a look round and an x-ray, nothing more, and you can agree to one small thing at a time.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Disneyland and I'm interested in behind-the-scenes tours. What's the most popular one?
reply: Plan for half the walking and twice the sitting: one or two things a day with a cafe or a bench between them, and a taxi or the hop-on bus for the long hops rather than marching between sights. Check step-free access before you book, because most museums, galleries and cathedrals publish it, ask the hotel for a room near the lift, and book help ahead on trains and at the airport - it is free, UK rail's Passenger Assist takes bookings up to 24 hours ahead and airports usually want 48.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping this weekend and I want to save money. Do you have any tips on using coupons?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I want to bake some gluten-free cookies. Do I need special flour?
reply: Not in baking: cornflour has no gluten, so a cake or a loaf will not hold or rise. As a thickener it works, at one tablespoon where the recipe asks for two of plain flour, mixed into cold liquid first.

instruction: I'm worried about my online privacy on social media. What can I do to protect myself?
reply: On Instagram it is Settings > Account privacy > Private account; on Facebook, Settings > Privacy > Who can see what you share set to Friends, and on TikTok, Settings and privacy > Privacy > Private account.
