instruction: I want to bake a cake, but I don't have a mixer. Can I still make it?
reply: You can cut the sugar in most cakes and traybakes by a third to a half and still get a good bake, but not all of it: sugar keeps the crumb soft, browns the crust and holds the structure, so a cake with none bakes pale, dry and crumbly. Leave at least a quarter of what the recipe asks, add a splash of milk if the batter looks stiff, and eat it within a couple of days.

instruction: I'm planning to cook dinner for my family tonight. What's a good dish to make for a special occasion?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics in school. What is DNA?
reply: DNA is the long molecule that carries the instructions for building and running a living thing, written in a four-letter code. Genes are sections of it, and they are copied from parents to offspring.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my coworkers at the office. Do you have any tips for improving my communication skills?
reply: Give the day a shape: same start time, dressed, a real lunch away from the desk, and a walk to end it. Put the phone in another room for one 50-minute block before you open email, and have one call with a colleague a day - the office is what you are missing, so put a bit of it back in the week.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm thinking of taking a nap. What's the ideal nap duration?
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering what the periodic table is.
reply: There are 118 elements in order of atomic number, and Mendeleev put the first table together in 1869 leaving gaps for elements nobody had found yet. For school you need the first 20 by heart: hydrogen, helium, lithium, beryllium, boron, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine, neon, sodium, magnesium, aluminium, silicon, phosphorus, sulfur, chlorine, argon, potassium, calcium.

instruction: I've been wondering, is verbal communication more important than non-verbal?
reply: Understand more before you try to speak, and speak badly early: ten minutes of listening or reading you mostly follow, every day, does more in a month than a grammar book. Learn whole phrases rather than single words - "could I have...", "I've just..." - because they come out in the right order without you building them.

instruction: What is a carton used for?
reply: Most of it is air and packaging: flatten cartons, crush cans and squash bottles with the lid off, and the same bag holds twice as much. Put a smaller bin by the counter and take it out every night rather than waiting for the big one to fill, and keep a caddy beside it for peelings, which is often a third of the weight.

instruction: I'm planning to visit the mall this weekend. What are some common types of anchor stores?
reply: Look for the places that sell a lot of one thing: a market hall or a food court, a bakery, a cafe at the back of a shop, a street food van in a regular spot, or the lunch board outside a restaurant that wants the office trade. Walk a street back from the station or the main road, where the rents are lower, and follow the queue of people who work nearby.

instruction: I'm interested in the Olympics. Have there been any controversies?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: What's the difference between weight and mass?
reply: BMI stands for body mass index: weight in kilos divided by height in metres squared, with 18.5 to 24.9 called healthy for most adults. It is a rough measure - it cannot tell muscle from fat, so it reads high on a rugby player and low on some older people, which is why waist size is worth knowing too.

instruction: I'm thinking of making some home improvements, but I'm not sure if I should do it myself or hire a professional.
reply: Yes, usually by a third to a half, and the older the thing gets the better the saving: furniture, bikes, tools, a pram, kids' clothes and kitchen kit lose most of their value in the first year and then almost nothing. Buy new the things that wear unseen or are used against your body - a mattress, running shoes, a bike helmet, anything with a safety job (a car seat, a life jacket, a smoke alarm) - and buy new where a warranty is what you are really paying for, like a laptop or a washing machine.

instruction: I'm looking for a new scarf. What are some popular colors for scarves this season?
reply: Familiar, subdued clothes are the thing: black or dark colours, smart and comfortable, and nothing new needed. If the family asked for bright colours or a football shirt, follow that instead, because it's about them.

instruction: What is a canyon?
reply: A rock is a solid piece of the earth made of one or more minerals: granite is mostly quartz and feldspar, and limestone is mostly calcite. Rocks come in three kinds - igneous from cooled magma, sedimentary from settled layers, and metamorphic changed by heat and pressure.

instruction: I'm looking for a new book to read. What are some popular fiction genres?
reply: Yes, it counts. Comics, graphic novels, magazines and audio books all build the same thing a book does - the habit and the vocabulary - and a child who reads what they like reads far more of it than one handed a book they do not.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my remote team. Do you have any tips?
reply: Give the day a hard edge and keep it the same one: laptop shut and work phone in a drawer at a fixed time, then something physical - a walk, a shower, cooking - because the body changes gear more reliably than the mind. Tell your team the hours once, in writing: "I'm offline after 6 and I pick up messages at 9." If you work from the room you live in, put the laptop out of sight at the end of the day; a screen in the corner is a shift that never ends.

instruction: I'm looking for some new winter clothes. What's in style this season?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What are some common painting mediums?
reply: Before paint you need filler for the holes, fine sandpaper, masking tape, a dust sheet, a roller and tray, a brush for edges and an old screwdriver to open the tin. One litre of emulsion covers about 12 square metres, so measure the walls and buy two coats' worth.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm not sure if I'm sleeping enough. How many hours of sleep should I get each night?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm looking for a new coffee maker for my kitchen. What types are available?
reply: Fresh beans ground just before you brew, and a scale: 60g of coffee per litre for filter, or 18g in a double espresso. Stale grounds or a brew too weak to taste is what makes home coffee thin next to a cafe's.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of casual shoes, do you have any suggestions?
reply: Smart casual usually means dark jeans or trousers with a collared shirt or a nice top, and clean shoes: tidy, no tie. If you're unsure, dress one step smarter than you think and ask the host.

instruction: I'm looking for deals on laptops. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: A laptop if you will be typing - email, essays, spreadsheets, work - and a tablet if it is mostly reading, video, calls and games on the sofa. A tablet with a keyboard costs about what a laptop does and types worse, so make it the only machine only if you truly do not type; a cheap laptop and a 300 pound tablet side by side covers the most ground for the money.

instruction: I'm going to take the train to visit my family. Is train travel safe?
reply: Give them a fact rather than a reassurance: "I'll text you when I'm on the train" works where "don't worry" does not, because a worry needs something to hold. Ask what exactly they are afraid of, answer that one thing once, and then stop explaining - saying it a second and third time is what teaches them the worry is worth asking about.

instruction: I'm looking for a new workspace. What are some popular types of workspaces?
reply: A laptop if you will be typing - email, essays, spreadsheets, work - and a tablet if it is mostly reading, video, calls and games on the sofa. A tablet with a keyboard costs about what a laptop does and types worse, so make it the only machine only if you truly do not type; a cheap laptop and a 300 pound tablet side by side covers the most ground for the money.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting some smart home devices, but I'm worried about my privacy. Are smart speakers always listening?
reply: A smart plug goes between the socket and the thing, and you switch it from an app or by voice; it is the cheapest way to make a lamp, a fan or a Christmas tree smart. Check it is rated for what you plug in (13A for a heater, and never for anything that must not be cut off, like an iron or an electric blanket) and that it works with what you already have, Alexa or Google or Apple Home.

instruction: I'm a big sports fan. What are some local teams in the Boston area?
reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I'm trying to reduce my waste at home. What are some common items that can be recycled?
reply: The council's green bin is the cheapest route if you have one - many charge for the subscription and collect fortnightly - and the tip has a green waste skip. Grass, leaves and prunings can go in a compost bin at home too, but leave out cooked food, weeds in seed and anything diseased.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my team at work. We're not communicating well.
reply: Keep it short, warm and about you: "I had a lovely time, but I don't think we're a match - good luck with it." Send it as soon as you know rather than leaving them guessing, and pick a reason that closes the door: "I'm not feeling it" ends it, while "I'm really busy at work" invites another try. Don't offer friendship or a drink "some time" unless you mean it, and there is nothing to apologise for beyond one short sorry - wanting to stop is allowed, and a clean no is kinder than a slow fade.

instruction: I was wondering, what is the Earth's magnetic field?
reply: The Earth is layered: a thin rocky crust, a hot slow-flowing mantle, a liquid outer core of iron and nickel, and a solid inner core. The churning iron outer core is what makes the magnetic field that keeps the solar wind off us.

instruction: What's the temperature outside?
reply: Aim for 15 to 25C by day: open the vents and the door at about 25C, and shut them again mid-afternoon so the heat is kept for the night, because a closed greenhouse is 5 to 10C warmer than the air outside. Tomatoes, cucumbers and peppers stop growing below about 12C and set no fruit below 15C, so a heater set to 10 to 12C keeps them alive rather than growing, and a max-min thermometer in the shade inside tells you what your own greenhouse is really doing.

instruction: I'm looking for some home cardio exercises to do. What are some good options?
reply: Two or three sessions a week of five moves covers the whole body at home: squats or sit-to-stands for legs, press-ups (hands on a worktop if needed) for chest and arms, a row pulling a loaded bag or a band towards you for the back, glute bridges for hips, and a plank for the middle. Do two or three sets of eight to twelve, and add a little each week - more reps, a slower lower, a heavier bag - because muscle only grows when the last rep is hard.

instruction: I'm interested in playing music. Do you know what equipment I would need to get started?
reply: That is what headphones, a mute or a practice room are for, and most of it is cheaper than a row: a headphone amp for an electric guitar, a soundhole cover or a folded cloth in an acoustic, a practice mute for a violin or a brass instrument, and headphones on a digital piano. Pick the hours you would want quiet in yourself - not before nine and not after ten - and tell them once, cheerfully, that you play and when you stop.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What is protein used for in the body?
reply: Protein is a building material made of chains of amino acids: the body uses it to build and repair muscle, skin, hair and organs, and enzymes are proteins too. Meat, fish, eggs, milk, beans, lentils, nuts and tofu are good sources.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to stay fit at home, do you have any suggestions?
reply: For two or three nights: one change of clothes plus a layer, one pair of comfortable walking shoes, toiletries in a bag, phone charger and any tickets. Roll clothes to fit more in, and leave the "just in case" outfit at home.

instruction: I'm going to a music festival this weekend. What are some basic safety tips I should know?
reply: Nothing new on the day: the shoes, socks and kit you did your long runs in, plus your race number, safety pins, a bottle, and the gels or sweets you have practised with. Eat the breakfast you have tested, get there an hour early, and set off slower than feels right.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas to decorate my living room. I want to add some plants.
reply: Emulsion for walls and ceilings: matt for a bedroom or a living room, and a washable matt or eggshell where it has to take scrubbing, such as a hallway, a kitchen or a kids' room. Woodwork wants eggshell or satinwood rather than gloss, because gloss shows up every lump and brush mark.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of jeans. What are the current styles?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm worried about my dog's weight. He's been gaining a lot lately.
reply: Most dogs that seem permanently hungry are simply greedy, and it is no sign that anything is wrong: weigh the day's food on the kitchen scale against the amount on the bag for his weight, split it into two meals, and slow him down with a puzzle bowl or a scatter feed. Go to the vet if the weight is dropping, if he has started drinking a lot, or if the hunger came on with a change of food - worms, a gut problem and diabetes all look like this.

instruction: What is the difference between a meter and a yard?
reply: A smart meter is the gas and electricity meter that sends your readings to your supplier itself, so nobody has to read it and the bill is based on what you used rather than an estimate. It comes with a small display for the kitchen that shows what you are spending as you use it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I'm planning to start playing basketball again after a long break. What are some common injuries I should watch out for?
reply: Fitness and touch come back at different speeds, and it is the second one that gets people hurt. Train twice a week for a fortnight before you play any match at all, then a half, then a full one - about six weeks from the first session to playing as you did.

instruction: I'm looking to start a board game collection. What are some popular board games for beginners?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: I'm looking for a new song to listen to. What's a popular song right now?
reply: *Song Exploder* takes one song and has the person who made it pull it apart, track by track, in 20 minutes. *Desert Island Discs* is the long interview with the music choices in it, and *All Songs Considered* is the weekly new-music one.

instruction: I'm starting a compost pile in my backyard. What can I put in it?
reply: Compost is plant waste that has rotted down into dark crumbly stuff that smells of earth: layer green things like grass, peelings and weeds with brown things like cardboard, dead leaves and twiggy prunings, keep it as damp as a wrung-out sponge, and turn it now and then. Six months to a year and it is ready to spread on beds or dig in, and it feeds the soil rather than the plant.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school, and I was wondering how seeds get dispersed.
reply: Plants take up water through their roots, and it is pulled up narrow tubes in the stem by evaporation from the leaves. That is why a cut flower wilts and why overwatering drowns roots that need air.

instruction: I'm going to a concert tonight and I'm planning to take some photos. Do you have any tips for concert photography?
reply: Guests usually go smart: a dress or a shirt and trousers with closed shoes, and a layer, because gowns and halls are either freezing or stuffy. Flats or a wide heel are kinder if the photos are on grass.

instruction: I'm thinking of buying a new car and I'm considering an electric vehicle. What are the main benefits of electric cars?
reply: An electric car drives like an automatic with one difference: when you lift off the accelerator it slows itself down and puts charge back in the battery, so you brake with the right pedal for most stops and use the left one only for a hard stop. Treat the range as about 70% of the official figure in winter, charge to 80% for everyday use and 100% only before a long run, and check the car's own route planner for chargers rather than arriving on 5%.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Hawaii and I'm looking for a vacation rental. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Pick one shape and put a time on it, because a free day with no plan turns into the sofa. The ones that cost nothing: a walk with a destination (a park, a canal, a hill, a shop that sells something you like), a free museum or gallery - most have a permanent collection that costs nothing - and the library, which has events, papers and warmth.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for summer meals. What are some popular seasonal ingredients?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm a parent and I'm looking for ideas for a school fundraiser. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Ring the charity shop before you load the car: most take a bag or two of books and say no to a bootful, and a book bank at the tip or a supermarket car park takes as many as you have. Paperbacks go down well at a hospital, a care home or a phone box library, and a school fair clears children's books.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, can I buy it online from your store?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's the difference between pop and rock music?
reply: A rock is a solid piece of the earth made of one or more minerals: granite is mostly quartz and feldspar, and limestone is mostly calcite. Rocks come in three kinds - igneous from cooled magma, sedimentary from settled layers, and metamorphic changed by heat and pressure.

instruction: I'm learning about adaptation and evolution in school. What's the difference between them?
reply: Natural selection is how evolution works: individuals vary, the ones whose variations suit their surroundings have more surviving young, and those variations become common over generations. It is not a plan or a choice - the environment simply filters what is already there.

instruction: I want to learn about ecosystems. What is an ecosystem?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm running low on shampoo. What are some key things to look for when buying a new one?
reply: Vacuum it first, then test any shampoo or foam cleaner on a hidden patch: a carpet wants a carpet shampoo worked in with a brush and rinsed, or a hired machine once or twice a year, and a sofa wants a foam cleaner and a soft brush with as little water as you can manage. Open the windows and dry it with the heating low, because anything left damp smells.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my video calls. The quality is really bad.
reply: Sit closer to the router or use a cable, and shut the other heavy things on the laptop: a browser with twenty tabs is usually the cause of a freezing call. Turn the video off when the sound matters more, and in Zoom or Teams set the video to a lower quality - a still picture and clear sound beats a frozen face.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet for my elderly mom. What kind of pet is good for seniors?
reply: It's a hard thing to watch, and being scared for him is part of loving an old dog. What helps most is a vet check now and every six months: pain relief for stiff joints, a senior food, and a plan for the bad days.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I want to make a shopping list. What's the best way to do that?
reply: A bucket list is the list of things you want to do before you die - the name comes from kick the bucket. It works better as ten or fifteen things with a date and a rough cost next to each than as a long wish list: one a year is a good pace, and putting the cheapest next keeps it moving.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier, but I love pizza. Are there any healthier alternatives to regular pizza?
reply: Cold pizza is fine if it went into the fridge within a couple of hours of arriving: eat it within 3 days, and reheat it to piping hot if you want it hot again - a splash of water in the pan or 10 minutes in a hot oven brings the base back. Pizza left out overnight is the one to throw away.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure what electronics to pack.
reply: Pack what you use least first - books, spare bedding, the cupboard under the stairs - and keep a 'first night' box out of the van: kettle, mugs, chargers, loo roll, bedding and a change of clothes. Label boxes by room, do one room an evening for the last three weeks, and get rid of anything you have not touched in a year rather than paying to move it.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different cultural foods. Can you tell me about Japanese food?
reply: Fish and chips feeds a group for the least money and nobody argues about it. If tastes differ, Indian beats Chinese: more vegetarian mains, and the sides stretch, so two mains with one rice and one bread feeds three.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes. What are some popular options?
reply: Wear the version of your usual clothes that you feel best in, clean and comfortable, and skip anything you'd be tugging at all evening. A jacket over a nice top covers a cold walk and a warm bar, and flat or low shoes leave you free to walk somewhere else.

instruction: I'm looking for a new book to read. What are some popular literary awards?
reply: Reading on paper in low light is one of the better wind-downs there is, and a book you have read before is easier to put down than a new one. It is the backlit screen and the scrolling that delay sleep, so a phone or tablet story is the one to move; an e-reader on a warm setting is much closer to paper.

instruction: I was wondering, why do we have seasons on Earth?
reply: Seasons come from the Earth's 23.5-degree tilt, not from how close it is to the sun. When your half of the planet leans towards the sun you get summer: longer days and more direct light.

instruction: I want to gain muscle, what should I eat?
reply: Only if you struggle to hit the number with meals: a shake is convenient protein, not a shortcut, and food does the same job for less money. If you do buy one, a plain whey or a plant blend is fine - one scoop after training covers 20 to 25g - and the timing barely matters, because the total for the day is what builds muscle.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body. What are the five senses?
reply: The brain is a network of about 86 billion nerve cells that talk to each other through electrical and chemical signals. Different regions handle different jobs - movement, sight, language, emotion and memory - and the connections between them are what let you think, learn and remember; it runs on about 20 percent of the body's energy.

instruction: I'm going to graduate soon and I was wondering, what's the significance of turning the tassel during the graduation ceremony?
reply: It means starting before the right moment. What are you about to do early?

instruction: I'm hungry, what are some quick meal ideas?
reply: Start small and gentle: a piece of fruit, a yoghurt or a slice of toast, then wait twenty minutes before a proper meal. Fat, sugar and coffee on an empty stomach are what make people feel sick, shaky and headachy, so go easy on those and have a glass of water first.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, but I don't know where to start. I love baking, but I want to reduce the sugar in my recipes.
reply: Nothing is banned: it is the size of the starchy and sugary part that counts. Make half the plate vegetables, a quarter meat, fish, eggs or beans and a quarter potatoes, rice, pasta or bread, wholegrain where you can, because it lifts your sugar more slowly.

instruction: I'm looking for a new smartphone. What are some popular brands?
reply: Most phones get security updates for five to seven years from new - an iPhone around five or six, a Samsung flagship about four, a cheap Android two or three - so a phone keeps working well for about four years, and the battery is usually what gives out first. A £50 to £90 battery swap buys two or three more years, which is far cheaper than a new handset.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I want to take some amazing photos and videos. Do you have any tips for travel photography?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What are some common sleep aids?
reply: Sleeping on your side, cutting out alcohol in the evening and losing a little weight fix it for most people who snore, and a blocked nose is worth treating with a decongestant or a steroid spray from the chemist for a couple of weeks to see. A pillow that keeps you off your back, or a tennis ball sewn into the back of a top, does the side-sleeping job.

instruction: I'm a big fan of basketball. Who's your favorite basketball player?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm worried about my cat's upcoming vet visit. What can I expect?
reply: From about eight, twice a year is worth it: the vet can find the things old cats hide — kidney trouble, thyroid, arthritis, high blood pressure — before you see them. Weigh her monthly at home and ask for a blood and urine test at the annual visit.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about basketball. What's the objective of the game?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm interested in starting yoga. What are the main benefits?
reply: Pilates is the better pick for a weak or sore back and a strong middle - it is slow, controlled work on the deep stomach and hip muscles - and yoga is the better pick for flexibility, balance and winding down. Both are low-impact and fine to start from nothing, so if the choice is still even, take the one whose teacher you liked.

instruction: I'm looking for a full-body workout routine to do at home. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Two or three sessions a week of five moves covers the whole body at home: squats or sit-to-stands for legs, press-ups (hands on a worktop if needed) for chest and arms, a row pulling a loaded bag or a band towards you for the back, glute bridges for hips, and a plank for the middle. Do two or three sets of eight to twelve, and add a little each week - more reps, a slower lower, a heavier bag - because muscle only grows when the last rep is hard.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to exercise my dog. What are some good pet-friendly parks and trails near me?
reply: Dogs dig out of boredom, heat or the smell of something buried, so give it a spot of its own — a sandpit with toys buried in it — and reward digging there. Cover the rest with stones or a mesh, keep it exercised and never shout when it's already dug.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about traffic calming measures. What are some common types?
reply: Confidence comes from the route, not the traffic: ride the quiet-street version at a weekend, then take it on a weekday at a quieter hour, and repeat until the turns are automatic. Ride a door's width out from parked cars, take the middle of the lane at junctions so nobody squeezes past, and look back before you move over.

instruction: I'm looking for information about pet food for my dog. What types of commercial pet foods are available?
reply: Plain peanut butter is fine for most dogs in small amounts, but check the label for xylitol, which is poisonous to them. Keep it to a teaspoon as a treat, and skip it if the dog is overweight.

instruction: I'm going to the airport tomorrow and I'm thinking of taking a taxi. Do I need to book in advance?
reply: Plan for half the walking and twice the sitting: one or two things a day with a cafe or a bench between them, and a taxi or the hop-on bus for the long hops rather than marching between sights. Check step-free access before you book, because most museums, galleries and cathedrals publish it, ask the hotel for a room near the lift, and book help ahead on trains and at the airport - it is free, UK rail's Passenger Assist takes bookings up to 24 hours ahead and airports usually want 48.

instruction: I'm a little worried about my cat. She's been acting weird lately and I don't know what's wrong.
reply: Look for what has changed rather than for crying: hiding, sitting hunched with her head low, no longer jumping up where she used to, over-grooming one spot, eating less, or going outside the tray. Cats purr when they are in pain as well as when they are content, so a purring cat is not a comfortable one.

instruction: I'm looking for a new yoga mat. What should I consider when choosing one?
reply: Pilates is the better pick for a weak or sore back and a strong middle - it is slow, controlled work on the deep stomach and hip muscles - and yoga is the better pick for flexibility, balance and winding down. Both are low-impact and fine to start from nothing, so if the choice is still even, take the one whose teacher you liked.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping lately. Do you think it's because of the seasonal change?
reply: Feeling flat and tired in January or the dark months is common: less daylight shifts sleep and mood, and most people pick up by March. Get outside within an hour of waking, even on a grey day, keep up vitamin D in winter, and keep seeing people.

instruction: I'm interested in airplanes. What are some common types of aircraft?
reply: A wing is shaped so air moves faster over the top than underneath, and the pressure difference pushes the wing up; that force is called lift. Engines provide the forward thrust, and lift grows with speed until it beats the plane's weight.

instruction: I want to start playing basketball, what equipment do I need?
reply: Start with very little: trainers or astro boots, shorts or leggings, a water bottle and, for football or hockey, shin pads. Clubs lend sticks, bats and bibs to beginners, so email and ask what they provide before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm planning a barbecue this weekend and I'm not sure what type of grill to use.
reply: An oven grill wants about five minutes preheating with the door shut, with the shelf 10cm or so below the element: the element should be glowing red across its whole length, and a drop of water flicked at the pan should sizzle. Food that browns in a minute and stays raw inside means the shelf is too high, not that the grill is too hot.

instruction: I have a lot of homework tonight, and I'm feeling overwhelmed. Do you have any tips on how to manage my time?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm looking for a new online learning platform to improve my language skills. Have you heard of Duolingo?
reply: The Coffee Break series - Spanish, French, German, Italian - is the place to start: 15 to 20 minutes a lesson, from hello upwards. Then the Duolingo Spanish Podcast for real stories told slowly in Spanish with English in between, and *InnerFrench* once you can follow a two-minute story in French.

instruction: I'm thinking about my grandparents. What are some common roles grandparents play in their families?
reply: Be specific about what you need and when, and agree the basics up front: bedtimes, treats and what to do if the child is ill. Grandparents usually want to help and hate guessing, so a short 'could you do Tuesdays, and we do baths' beats hinting.

instruction: I'm planning to do some online shopping. How do I know if a website is secure?
reply: Leave it where people look, and where the business will see it: the order page for an online shop (that is the one the seller can answer), Google Maps for a cafe, shop or restaurant, TripAdvisor for a hotel. Three or four lines beat a rant - what you bought, when, what went wrong, and what you want - and give the stars you actually mean, since a 2 with a fair paragraph is read and a 1 with none is not.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet. What are some benefits of adopting a senior pet?
reply: It's a hard thing to watch, and being scared for him is part of loving an old dog. What helps most is a vet check now and every six months: pain relief for stiff joints, a senior food, and a plan for the bad days.

instruction: I'm trying to understand social media analytics better. What is the main purpose of it?
reply: It means getting to understand something that is not clicking yet. What is the thing?

instruction: I think I sprained my ankle. What should I do?
reply: An ankle that keeps rolling or giving way has usually left the ligaments loose after an old sprain, and the fix is strength and balance work rather than a support: stand on one leg with your eyes shut for a minute a day, do heel raises, and a physio can set you a short programme. Get it looked at if it swells up after each turn, locks, or you cannot put weight on it now.

instruction: I'm training for my first 5K run and I'm not sure how to start. What should I do first?
reply: A first 5k usually takes 30 to 40 minutes at a jog with walking breaks; the average parkrun time is about 28 minutes, and anything near 25 is quick. Walking the whole way is roughly 45 to 50 minutes, and most races allow far longer than that, so a first one is not something to worry about being slow at.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some healthy snacks?
reply: A 30g handful of nuts is about 175 calories and one of the better snacks you can buy: 6g of protein, 3g of fibre and fat that is mostly unsaturated, and people who eat them regularly tend to weigh less, not more, because they are satisfying. Walnuts are the one with omega-3 (plant ALA).

instruction: I'm interested in language and technology. What's the main goal of natural language processing?
reply: ICT stands for information and communication technology, the school subject that used to be called computer studies: word processing, spreadsheets, and how to search and check what you find. Schools now tend to call it computing, and teach programming in it as well.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's popular right now?
reply: *Song Exploder* takes one song and has the person who made it pull it apart, track by track, in 20 minutes. *Desert Island Discs* is the long interview with the music choices in it, and *All Songs Considered* is the weekly new-music one.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I need to make a list. Can you help me with that?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of dress shoes, do you have any recommendations?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure what toiletries to pack.
reply: Nappies and wipes, three or four babygrows and vests, maternity pads, your own toiletries and a phone charger with a long cable, plus snacks and a water bottle. Pack two bags - a small one for the labour room and a bigger one for the ward - and keep your notes and ID on the top of one, because someone asks for them at the door.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about black holes and neutron stars. What's the main difference between them?
reply: A black hole is a place where matter is packed so tightly that its gravity pulls in everything, even light. Most form when a very massive star runs out of fuel and collapses; we spot them by the way their gravity moves and heats nearby gas.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. Can you tell me what a normal sleep schedule is?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding some words in a book I'm reading. Can you help me?
reply: I cannot read it for you, but the check that catches most of it is reading it aloud: your ear stops on the missing word and the doubled one. Then look at four things in order - the name at the top, the ask in the first line, any number or date, and the last line.

instruction: What is a force in physics?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm boiling some potatoes, but I'm not sure how long they should cook for.
reply: Test them with a knife rather than a fork: it should slide in with no resistance at all and the potato should still hold its shape. Boiled, that is 10 to 12 minutes for small new potatoes, 15 to 20 for chunks and 20 to 25 for whole medium ones; a fork tells you too late, and a potato left a minute too long goes watery.

instruction: I'm learning about colors and their meanings. What does the color blue mean?
reply: It means it happened suddenly, with no warning. What came out of the blue?

instruction: I'm looking to buy some new clothes online. What shipping options do you have?
reply: Lay everything out and take half the clothes and twice the money: three tops, two bottoms, one warm layer and shoes you can walk in covers a week. Roll clothes, keep a change in your hand luggage, and buy anything you forget when you arrive.

instruction: I'm looking for a new watch. What are some popular types of watches right now?
reply: It depends on the crystal, and the make and model tell you which: acrylic or Hesalite (many older and cheaper watches) polishes out at home with a dab of Polywatch or Brasso on a soft cloth, a mineral glass one wants a jeweller with cerium oxide - about £15 to £30 - and a sapphire crystal only scratches on a diamond or a brick, so a mark that will not lift is usually the anti-reflective coating. A scratch you can feel with a fingernail is a new crystal, £30 to £80 fitted, and worth doing before damp gets in.

instruction: I'm worried about my computer getting a virus. What can I do to protect it?
reply: Malware is software written to do something you did not ask for: a virus that spreads, spyware that watches, ransomware that locks your files until you pay. It arrives as an attachment, a fake update or a program from a site that is not the maker's, so the protection that works is updating the system, keeping to official app stores and never opening a file you did not expect.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. Is it true that the Earth's temperature is rising?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school and I was wondering, what is a pulley?
reply: A pulley is a wheel with a rope running over it: one changes the direction of a pull, so you pull down to lift a load up, and two together halve the force you need by doubling the rope. That is why a flagpole and a crane both use one.

instruction: I'm planning a road trip from New York to Los Angeles. What are the main roads I'll be taking?
reply: The minimum is a front light of 500 lumens or more, a rear light, a gold-rated D-lock through the frame and a rack, a waterproof jacket and gloves. Plan a route on quieter roads or a cycle path, leave shoes and a change of clothes at work, and start with two days a week: six miles takes about half an hour at an easy pace.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet, but I'm not sure what kind to get.
reply: Ask in writing before you get the animal, because a tenancy that says no pets is a term you can ask to have changed but not one you can ignore: put the animal in the letter - the kind, its age, that it is house-trained and insured - offer to have the carpets cleaned when you leave and to put right anything it damages, and ask for a written answer. A landlord can say no, but in England a blanket ban with no way to ask is the kind of term consumer law lets you challenge, so a reasoned refusal in writing is worth having before you take it further.

instruction: I'm looking for some family dinner ideas. What's a popular meal that kids like?
reply: Mash them in rather than serve them whole: beans or lentils blended into a tomato sauce or a shepherd's pie disappear, and peas or sweetcorn folded through rice do too. Put the new thing next to something they already eat, no bargaining and no second dinner, and keep offering it - it can take eight or ten tries before a child accepts a food.

instruction: What is a cube?
reply: A cube is a solid with six square faces of the same size, twelve edges and eight corners: a sugar lump and a die are cubes. Its volume is the side multiplied by itself three times, so a 2 cm cube holds 8 cm³, and its surface area is six times one face.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm looking for a place to stay. What are my options?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm learning to play tennis. What is the most important part of a forehand shot?
reply: Badminton is won with the feet: after every shot get back to the middle of the court, and split-step as your opponent hits so you can move either way. Learn the overhead clear hit high and deep to the back line, then the drop shot from the same action, so your opponent cannot read it.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet, but I'm not sure if it's a good idea. What are some benefits of having a pet?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm thinking about remodeling my home. What are some rooms I should consider?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm looking for some new smoothie ideas. What are some popular fruits to use in smoothies?
reply: Five a day is real, and it is about 400g of fruit and vegetables rather than five items: a portion is 80g, which is one apple, three heaped tablespoons of peas, or a handful of grapes. A smoothie counts once however much of it you drink, and so does a 150ml glass of juice, because the fibre is broken up and it goes down too fast - whole fruit is better.

instruction: I'm having trouble reading my textbooks for school. Do you know any strategies that can help me?
reply: Find the first topic you stopped understanding rather than the newest one, because everything after it is built on it: go through the textbook contents or the topic list and mark the last thing that made sense. Then do three things - tell the teacher you have fallen behind and ask which two topics matter most for the next test, spend twenty minutes a day on those two only, and get one session with a classmate who is good at them.

instruction: My niece is graduating from high school soon. What are some common ways to celebrate this occasion?
reply: Make the gift something you do together: a picnic at the spot of your first date, a small photo book of the year, or a jar of twelve notes with one to open each month. The thought shows in the specifics, not the price.

instruction: I'm feeling tired lately. How many hours of sleep do I need each night?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm planning to grill some burgers this weekend. What's the best way to preheat the grill?
reply: An oven grill wants about five minutes preheating with the door shut, with the shelf 10cm or so below the element: the element should be glowing red across its whole length, and a drop of water flicked at the pan should sizzle. Food that browns in a minute and stays raw inside means the shelf is too high, not that the grill is too hot.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family traditions. What are some common family traditions during holidays?
reply: Two lines is plenty unless it is family: "Merry Christmas - hope the year has been kind to you and the next one is better." Add a specific thing you remember from the year for anyone close ("still laughing about the tent"), and for a neighbour or a colleague a plain wish and both your names is the whole job.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about app development. What programming languages are used for it?
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my camera settings. What's the difference between ISO and aperture?
reply: Close every other app that might be holding the camera, then check the permission: on Windows, Settings > Privacy & security > Camera, and on a Mac, System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera, and switch your app on. A laptop with a sliding shutter over the lens is the other common one.

instruction: I'm interested in astronauts. What do they do?
reply: There is gravity in space: astronauts on the space station float because they and the station are falling around the Earth together at the same speed, not because gravity has gone. At that height gravity is still about 90% as strong as it is on the ground.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about important inventions. What's one of the most important inventions in history?
reply: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone and got the key patent in 1876, though Antonio Meucci had demonstrated a working voice device years earlier. Bell's patent, and the company built on it, is why his name stuck.

instruction: I'm looking to start a home gym and I'm not sure what equipment to get. What's the difference between dumbbells and barbells?
reply: Buy one adjustable dumbbell or one kettlebell and nothing else to begin with: about 6 to 10 kg suits most beginners and 10 to 16 kg if you are already strong, and a used one goes for £40 to £80. Add a resistance band for about £10 and a step or a sturdy chair, and that covers squats, rows, presses and carries - a mat only if your floor is hard.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm worried about fleas and ticks. What can I do to prevent them?
reply: Fleas are not a sign of a dirty house: they come in on the animal and the eggs drop into the carpet, so the house is the part that keeps them coming back. Treat the animal and the house on the same day: a spot-on or tablet from the vet for every pet, bedding washed at 60C, and the carpets vacuumed daily for a fortnight, emptying the vacuum outside, because most of a flea infestation is eggs and pupae in the floor, not fleas on the pet.

instruction: I'm looking for some discounts on electronics. Are there any flash sales happening?
reply: Ring or log in and ask why it went up and from which date: it is usually the end of a fixed deal, a meter estimate instead of a reading, or a price rise the supplier has to tell you about in advance. Give an up-to-date reading, and if the tariff ended, switch rather than stay on the standard one - for a phone or broadband, ask for the retentions team and say you are leaving, which is where the discounts are.

instruction: I'm a bit worried about the weather forecast. Is a thunderstorm expected today?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm looking for information about theater productions in my city. Are there any musicals playing right now?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding what I read. Do you have any tips for improving my reading comprehension?
reply: Understand more before you try to speak, and speak badly early: ten minutes of listening or reading you mostly follow, every day, does more in a month than a grammar book. Learn whole phrases rather than single words - "could I have...", "I've just..." - because they come out in the right order without you building them.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school and I was wondering, what are the six types of simple machines?
reply: Do them out loud, in order, then shuffled, in two-minute bursts a few times a day - short and often beats long and rare. Learn the easy ones first (2s, 5s, 10s, then the squares) so more than half the table is familiar.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow. What should I do to prepare?
reply: Book the check-up and say on the phone that you are nervous and have not been for a while - practices hear it every week, and most will give you a longer first appointment, a signal to stop, and no lecture. The first visit is usually a look round and an x-ray, nothing more, and you can agree to one small thing at a time.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I want to try meditation, but I don't know where to start.
reply: Meditation is paying attention to one thing on purpose - usually the breath - and coming back to it each time you notice you have drifted; an empty mind is not the aim, and the noticing is the skill. The tested versions are the eight-week courses, MBSR and MBCT, mainly for low mood and anxiety.

instruction: I'm looking for a new baking tool. What is a pastry brush used for?
reply: A pastry brush is the small brush for glazing and greasing: beaten egg on a pie lid, milk on a bun, melted butter in a tin, a wash of syrup on a warm cake. Silicone takes the heat and washes clean; a bristle brush gives a finer finish but sheds, so keep it for cool jobs.

instruction: I'm a bit worried about the storm forecast this weekend. How do storms get their names?
reply: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat in the atmosphere instead of letting it escape to space. That extra heat raises average temperatures, melts ice and makes extreme weather more likely; the science is settled, though predicting any one storm is not.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my home's heating and cooling system. What are some basic things I can do to maintain it?
reply: Condensation comes from warm wet air hitting cold surfaces, so ventilate and keep the place a bit warmer: use the extractor fan, open a window for 10 minutes a day, dry clothes outside or in a vented dryer, and leave the heating on low rather than off and on. A dehumidifier helps in a bedroom that gets it badly.

instruction: I'm looking for information about plants. What are some popular types of houseplants?
reply: A houseplant that will not flower is usually short of light or being fed too much: most of them need a bright spot with a few hours of sun a day to set buds, and a feed high in nitrogen grows leaves at the flowers' expense, so switch to a tomato feed with more potash in late summer. Peace lilies and Christmas cacti also want cooler nights and a slightly pot-bound root to be nudged into flower; African violets want the light and nothing else changed.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What is it?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a smart speaker for my home. What's the difference between Amazon Echo and Google Home?
reply: Press the microphone button on the speaker: on an Echo it is the circle with a line through it on top, and it glows red when the mics are off; a Google Home or Nest has a switch at the back. Nothing is recorded while it is off, and in the Alexa app, Settings > Alexa Privacy > Review Voice History lets you delete what it already has.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness app to help me stay active. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Pick one thing and do it every week rather than signing up to three apps: a class, a club, a walking group, or a single app you actually answer. Say early what you are looking for, meet in daylight for something short - a coffee, not dinner - and tell a friend where you will be.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening. What is organic gardening?
reply: Rosemary, thyme and oregano are bought as small plants or grown from softwood cuttings in summer, not from seed: seed is slow and comes up uneven. They want sun, very free drainage - grit in the compost, or a gravel mulch - and far less water than basil; a woody herb in wet soil rots at the base.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'd like to know some relaxation techniques. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm planning to go to the mall with my kids this weekend. What are some tips for shopping with children?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm trying to save money on groceries. Is buying in bulk a good idea?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I want to get in shape, what are some good sports to try?
reply: A sports bra is a bra built to hold the breast still rather than shape it, and the amount it holds is graded: low support for yoga and walking, medium for cycling and weights, high for running and anything bouncy. Buy it by the band size rather than the cup alone - it should be snug on the loosest hook with two fingers of room under the band - and replace it when the band has stretched, usually after about a year of regular washing.

instruction: I need a quick weeknight meal idea. What's something simple I can make?
reply: Cook one meal and serve it in parts, keeping the sauce, the vegetables and the meat apart, so the parts that are not wanted can be left without it being a scene. Say the thing you actually need once, at a calm moment rather than over the plate: one night a week they cook, or they sort their own dinner on the nights they do not want what is on.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about theater history. Can you tell me when the first theater was built?
reply: The Middle Ages are the centuries between the fall of Rome and the Renaissance, roughly 500 to 1500, and in England they start with the Norman Conquest in 1066. Most people farmed, the Church ran schools and hospitals, and castles, cathedrals and the first universities were built.

instruction: I'm feeling sad because my pet passed away recently. I'm missing them a lot.
reply: Say the plain thing and then be quiet: "I'm so sorry - I don't have words, but I'm here." Name the person who died if they have named them, say their name back, and offer one concrete thing instead of "let me know if you need anything": a lift, a meal on Thursday, sitting with them. Do not explain, compare it to your own loss, or look for the bright side; the comfort is in staying, and in being the one who is still there in three weeks.

instruction: I'm planning a family picnic this weekend. What are some popular family meal ideas?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. What are some popular types of cakes?
reply: Bake something that is low in sugar by nature rather than swapping in sweeteners: an almond and olive oil cake, a carrot cake made with less sugar and more spice, or berries with cream and a little dark chocolate. Keep the portion small and have it after a meal rather than on its own, and put the fruit and the cream on the plate so the cake slice can be thinner.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family. What are grandparents?
reply: Be specific about what you need and when, and agree the basics up front: bedtimes, treats and what to do if the child is ill. Grandparents usually want to help and hate guessing, so a short 'could you do Tuesdays, and we do baths' beats hinting.

instruction: I'm interested in gymnastics routines. What are the four events for women's artistic gymnastics?
reply: Women's matches at the Grand Slams are best of three sets and men's are best of five, except that most other tournaments are best of three for both. A set is first to six games, two clear.

instruction: I'm going to the theater for the first time, what are some basic rules I should follow?
reply: Ask other parents at the school gate first: a sitter vouched for by someone you know beats any app. Then do one evening while you are still in the house, paying them to play while you get on with something, so the first real night out isn't the first time.

instruction: I'm feeling sad because my family's old dog passed away yesterday. Do you have any advice on how to cope with the loss of a pet?
reply: It's a hard thing to watch, and being scared for him is part of loving an old dog. What helps most is a vet check now and every six months: pain relief for stiff joints, a senior food, and a plan for the bad days.

instruction: I'm learning about geology in school and I was wondering, what causes earthquakes?
reply: An earthquake is the ground shaking when two slabs of the Earth's crust slip past each other and the energy built up is released as waves. The slipping happens at a fault, and the shaking is strongest near it.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. What do plants need to grow?
reply: Plants need sunlight as the energy source for photosynthesis, the reaction that makes their food. Without enough light they cannot make sugar, so they stop growing and their leaves yellow and drop.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan soon and I want to take some great photos to share on social media.
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm having trouble getting my kids to bed on time. Do you have any tips for creating a sleep schedule for families?
reply: A toddler who goes down at seven and is awake again at ten is usually treating bedtime as a nap: push bedtime later by 15 minutes every few days, keep the room dark and the last hour quiet, and make the 10pm wake-up boring - a quick cuddle in the dark, no lights, no play. Ask your health visitor if it is still happening after two weeks.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise ball for my home workouts. What size should I get?
reply: Add weight when you can hit the top of your rep range on every set with clean form - usually every week or two when you are new. Take the smallest jump you have, 2.5kg on a bar or the next dumbbell up, and expect to lose a rep or two for a session or so; that is the new weight working, not a bad day.

instruction: I'm trying to get in shape and I'm looking for a good cardio workout.
reply: Do the one that is the point of the session first, because the second one gets the tired version of you: if you are there to get stronger, lift first and finish with ten minutes of cardio; if you are training for a run or a ride, do that first. Ten easy minutes on the bike before you lift is a warm-up, not cardio.

instruction: I'm thinking about taking some vitamins and supplements to improve my health. Are they safe?
reply: Most supplements are fine with most tablets: vitamin D, vitamin C, a multivitamin, cod liver oil and a probiotic can be taken alongside blood pressure tablets, statins, levothyroxine and antibiotics. The two that need care are vitamin K, which works against warfarin, and calcium or iron tablets, which want four hours between them and a thyroid tablet.

instruction: I'm looking for music classes for my kids. What are some popular options?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. What is the main part of a plant that makes food?
reply: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis: they take carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil and use sunlight to turn them into sugar. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light, and oxygen is released as a by-product.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is runoff?
reply: Precipitation is water falling out of the sky - rain, snow, sleet or hail - when droplets in a cloud join up until they are too heavy to stay up. It is one step of the water cycle, after evaporation and condensation.

instruction: I'm feeling tired lately and I'm not sure if I'm sleeping enough. How much sleep do adults need?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm planning a local trip this weekend and I'm looking for some historical sites to visit. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a smartwatch. What's the main purpose of a smartwatch?
reply: A smart meter is the gas and electricity meter that sends your readings to your supplier itself, so nobody has to read it and the bill is based on what you used rather than an estimate. It comes with a small display for the kitchen that shows what you are spending as you use it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new walking trail near my home. Do you know of any?
reply: Go for a canal towpath, a country park or a flat riverside path: wide, level, benches along it and nothing to climb over, which is what a short walk needs. Check the surface and the slope on the site's own page before you set off, because a walk advertised as circular can still hide a stile or a flight of steps, and ring ahead if someone uses a wheelchair - big attractions, National Trust and English Heritage places among them, lend one for free if it is booked a day or two in advance.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening. What are some basic garden tools I'll need?
reply: Tidy the outline first, because a garden reads as untidy at its edges before its middle: cut the lawn edge right round with a half-moon edger, clear the path, and weed the first foot of border. Then buy three plants and no more - something tall, something scented by the door, and something that flowers for months - in pots if the soil is poor.

instruction: I'm concerned about internet censorship. What is it?
reply: The internet is millions of computers agreeing on one way to pass messages - your request is cut into small packets, each labelled with where it is going, and routers hand them on hop by hop until they reach the server. Long fibre cables under the sea carry it between countries, and the reply usually takes well under a tenth of a second.

instruction: I'm planning to make some fried chicken for dinner, but I'm not sure what oil to use.
reply: Olive oil or rapeseed oil is a good everyday choice: both are high in unsaturated fat and fine for normal frying. Save the extra virgin olive oil for salads and low heat, and use a plain vegetable oil when you need a very hot pan.
